title: Bechukotai: I will walk among you (Leviticus 26:12)
hookLine: the promise is closeness: "I will walk among you"

lines: THE LAST WISH IN THE RUN.
cards: A good wedding toast builds. One wish, then another, each a little warmer, and the room waits for the big finish. The blessings in Leviticus twenty-six build the same way.
Bread to the full. Sleep with no one to make you afraid. By the end, a listener might expect the biggest wish of all to be something you could weigh, or count, or lock in a barn.
The last one in the run can't be stored. It's company. Yesterday the people walked in God's statutes.

teach.b: Leviticus twenty-six, verses eleven and twelve. First, God says the sanctuary will be set among the people. Then: "And I will walk among you, and will be your God, and ye shall be My people."
The Hebrew verb is v'hithalachti, a form that means walking about, strolling, going to and fro. Not a march: the walk of someone at home.
The same form appears in Genesis, where God is heard walking in the garden in the cool of the day. The Sifra, and Rashi after it, make the link out loud.
I will stroll with you in the garden, God says, as one of you, and you won't tremble before Me. Closeness without terror.
That's a surprising promise in a book full of fire and holy boundaries, where even the high priest is warned not to walk into the inner room whenever he likes. The next verse finishes the thought.
I broke the bars of your yoke, God says, and made you walk upright.
The people who once walked bent under Egyptian loads now walk with their heads up, and God walks among them. So the blessing at the top of the list isn't a thing. It's a relationship.
The harvest is good. Company on the road is better.

how: Jewish tradition reads Leviticus 26:12 as a promise of God's closeness; the Sifra's reading, that God will walk with the people as one of them and they will not be afraid, is often taught alongside the verse.

it says the opposite: God walks as one of them, and they won't be afraid.

games.q: Leviticus 26 has listed rain, fruit, plenty and peace. what does the run of blessings build to?
games.why: "and I will walk among you, and will be your God, and ye shall be My people." the top blessing is a relationship, not a thing.

practice: Close your eyes, or soften them, and walk your street in your mind: the curb, the corner, the house with the loud dog, the bus stop. Where on that ordinary route have you seen kindness, beauty, patience, someone helping someone?
If you pray, hold those places in that prayer; if you don't, simply notice that your street holds more than you usually see.

wordCard.voice: Bechukotai, the last portion of Leviticus. Its highest blessing: not a full barn, but God walking among the people, as one at home.
